fields.System.Title: OUT-3 — Waves
fields.System.Description:
Purpose

Group orders into batches of work released together, so pickers make one trip for twenty orders
instead of twenty trips.

Scope

In. Wave creation, workload preview, release, cancellation, auto-waving by cut-off,
blocking release on replenishment.

Out. The picking itself — that is [OUT-4](OUT-4-picking.md). Labour scheduling.

Design notes

Waves are pointless below a volume threshold. One pick task per order is correct at Stage 2.
Do not build this until order volume makes the trip saving real.

OUT-306 is the hardest coordination problem in the epic. Replenishment must complete
before the wave releases, or pickers hit empty pick faces mid-wave — which is worse than not
waving at all, because the work is already committed.

A released wave cannot be edited. Cancel and rebuild. Editing a wave whose tasks are
partly picked produces states nothing downstream handles.

Cancelling a wave must cancel its pick tasks and reset order state in one transaction.
Orphan pick tasks in a picker's list are confusing and get confirmed anyway.

Cap wave size by what can finish before the cut-off. A wave that cannot complete in time is
worse than no wave — the work is spread across every order instead of concentrated in the ones
that would have shipped.

Risks

| Risk | Reference |
|---|---|
| Replenishment not done before release | [doc 05 WF 5](../../../docs/05-workflows.md) |
| Wave too large to finish before cut-off | [doc 05 WF 5](../../../docs/05-workflows.md) |
| An order landing in two waves | [doc 05 WF 5](../../../docs/05-workflows.md) |
| Cancelling a wave leaving orphan tasks | [doc 05 WF 5](../../../docs/05-workflows.md) |
